***
You like a specific taste culture — not “nice portfolios” in general. Across all seven, the shared DNA is quiet confidence: the site proves skill by restraint, not by volume.

What’s common
1. The person is the product
None of these open like a generic agency site. It’s “I’m Eric,” “hola i’m pabs,” “Evil Rabbit is a designer…,” “john phamous.” Name, voice, and presence sit above role titles.

2. Extreme restraint
Especially Pablo, Pham, Logan, Evil Rabbit: narrow column, black/white, almost no chrome. The flex is “I don’t need a hero video.” Even the more visual ones (Eftakher, Eric, Dai) still feel edited, not stuffed.

3. Monochrome + type does the work
Near-black or near-white. Serif/sans mixes, or mono. Hierarchy from weight and spacing — not cards, gradients, or icon rows.

4. Design × engineering identity
Design engineers, “I ship in code,” components, systems, AI tools, Vercel orbit. You’re drawn to builders who make the site itself the proof, not just screenshots of Figma files.

5. Alive, current signals
Live clocks, location, “right now,” availability status, contribution graphs, “today / latest.” They feel like people who are currently shipping — not a frozen résumé from 2021.

6. Craft in the small things
Pill navs, hover underlines, theme toggles, ⌘K, name pronunciation, staggered fades, custom selection colors, playful easter eggs (Mello, obfuscated project names). Taste shows up in details, not decoration.

7. Pedigree stated calmly
Vercel, Auth0, NASA, acquisitions, angel checks — listed like facts, not trophies. Soft authority.

8. Personality without performing
Lowercase, dry humor, hobbies, side projects, essays. Human, but never try-hard or “fun startup” loud.

9. Systems over case-study theater
Components, design systems, creative tools, brand systems, AI products. Work about how things get made, not just “I redesigned a landing page.”

Why you like them so much
You’re responding to authored taste — sites that feel like one person’s hand, not a template.

You want the feeling of: this person is so good they can afford to be quiet. That quietness reads as status in the design-engineer world.

There’s a soft split in your list, but both sides feed the same craving:

Cluster	Sites	What hits you
Visual craft
Eftakher, Eric Sin, Dai
Grids, polish, beautiful work presentation, still restrained
Text as flex
Pablo, Pham, Logan, Evil Rabbit
Ultra-minimal CVs where confidence = subtraction
What you’re really attracted to isn’t “dark mode” or “minimalism” as trends. It’s:

Clarity over salesiness
Identity over portfolio theater
Craft over decoration
Builder energy over pure visual designer energy
Calm ego — strong presence without shouting
In one line: you like portfolios that feel like a signature, not a brochure.
***

if u want to take and and get their design systems. will u be able to do it? 
this is because, i really like how they all have made their portfolios, and i want to make mine like them. 

***
Yes — I can extract their design systems and turn that into something you can actually build from.

What I can pull from each site

Color tokens (bg, text, muted, borders, accents)
Typography (families, sizes, weights, line-height, tracking)
Spacing / layout (max-width, column width, section rhythm, grid)
Component patterns (nav, links, work lists, status pills, CTAs)
Motion (fade-ins, hovers, selection, transitions)
Voice/tone patterns (lowercase, first-person, “right now,” restraint)
How I’d use it for you

Extract systems from all 7
Distill the shared language (not 7 clones)
Build one your design system from that DNA
Apply it to your portfolio
What I won’t do is copy their logos, unique illustrations, or paste their code. You want the taste and structure, not a replica of one person’s site.

# Skill: caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

# Skill: frontend-skill-router

# Frontend skill router

Dispatcher only. Pick one **primary surface**, one **primary skill**, add
**modifiers**, then load the primary and work under it. All design work happens
inside the loaded skill; this router only routes.

Route on what the user is fundamentally trying to improve — the intended
artifact — not on every property the prompt mentions.

> **Invocation note (vs Matt’s glossary “Router Skill”):** Matt’s router
> archetype is **user-invoked** and indexes other user-invoked skills. This
> skill is **model-invoked** on purpose: its targets are model-invoked families
> that compete for attention, and AGENTS.md requires the agent to consult it
> first.

## Process

### 1. Pick the primary surface

Exactly one — surfaces answer “what interface is being designed”, nothing else:

| Primary surface | Signals | Primary skill |
|---|---|---|
| **Marketing** | Landing, portfolio, campaign/promo page, brand-forward or editorial site, “make it look better / not AI-generated” | `design-taste-frontend` |
| **Product** | App shell, dashboard, admin, settings, internal tool, SaaS UI, data-heavy workflow | `impeccable` (product register) |
| **Motion-first** | Motion itself is the deliverable: review/critique animations, fix springs or easing, design a gesture, tune a transition, implement an interaction | `emil-design-eng` |

Motion-first applies only when motion is the task. A marketing or product build
that merely contains animation keeps its Marketing/Product primary (motion
becomes a modifier in step 2).

Tie-break when several read applicable:

1. Motion-first, if motion is the deliverable
2. Product
3. Marketing

Examples:

| Request | Surface |
|---|---|
| “Landing page for a dashboard product” | Marketing |
| “Dashboard home page” | Product |
| “Animate my landing page” | Marketing (+ motion modifier) |
| “Review the animation on my landing page” | Motion-first |
| “Generate an image of a SaaS dashboard” | Product (image is output mode) |

**Done when:** one surface and its primary skill are named.

### 2. Add modifiers

Modifiers load secondary skills for a scoped subproblem; the primary keeps
ownership of the task.

| Modifier | When | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Motion | Marketing/Product task also needs meaningful motion | `emil-design-eng` — owns timing, springs, gestures, interaction feel only |
| Redesign | Improving an existing site/app | `redesign-existing-projects` |
| Motion critique | Reviewing existing animations | `review-animations` |
| Pattern naming | Naming or choosing a motion pattern | `animation-vocabulary` |
| Apple platform | iOS / macOS / visionOS / explicit HIG — any surface | `apple-design` |
| Complete large output | Task explicitly demands a full large implementation, or a previous output came back truncated (reactive load is fine) | `full-output-enforcement` |

**Output mode never changes ownership.** Code, image comp, mockup, or critique
is a delivery format: route by the interface first, then pick the tool — for
image output, use the Image row in [families.md](references/families.md).

**Done when:** primary plus all applicable secondaries are listed.

### 3. Apply the specialty override

Fires only when the brief **explicitly names** a Taste skin (brutalist,
minimal, high-end, stitch, gpt-taste); vague aesthetic language stays with the
generic primary.

| Surface | Named skin means |
|---|---|
| Marketing | The skin **replaces** `design-taste-frontend` as primary |
| Product | `impeccable` **stays primary**; the skin contributes style vocabulary only, and on any structural conflict (card nesting, radius, ghost-cards) Impeccable wins |
| Motion-first | Emil stays primary; the skin is ignored for ownership |

**Done when:** the override is applied, or you can state “no specialty named”.

### 4. Resolve conflicts

If two loaded families disagree on a topic, authority is per-topic — apply
[conflicts.md](references/conflicts.md); everything not listed there stays with
the primary. Quick precedence:

1. Interaction timing / easing / bounce / reduced-motion → **Emil**
2. Card structure on product UI → **Impeccable**
3. Marketing anti-slop / layout variance → **Taste**

**Done when:** each active disagreement resolves to one named winner.

### 5. Load and execute

1. Read the primary skill’s `SKILL.md` (and only the references it asks for).
2. Secondaries handle their scoped subproblem only — one primary family per pass.
3. Tell the user the route in one short line, then work under the primary.
4. Re-route only when the fundamental artifact changes (e.g. landing page →
   dashboard, or build → motion audit) — never per subtask.

**Done when:** the primary skill is loaded, secondaries are identified, the
route is stated, and work has started under the primary.

## Hard gates

| Prefer | Instead of |
|---|---|
| `design-taste-frontend` (v2) | `design-taste-frontend-v1` |
| One primary family per pass | Competing Taste / Impeccable / Emil primaries loaded as equals |
| Specialty skins only when the brief names them | Always-on Taste skins |
| Route, then design under the chosen skill | Designing inside this router |
